items.title: TRON’s recent numbers tell a bigger story than simple blockchain growth.
items.summary:
TRON’s recent numbers tell a bigger story than simple blockchain growth.

More than 400M total accounts, over $213M moved through TRON via WalletConnect in H1 2026, and more than $100M in swaps through deBridge within 30 days show an ecosystem increasingly connected to real capital flows.

The activity is also spreading across different layers of the network:

→ 1,221 apps across 185 countries connected through WalletConnect
→ $5M+ moved through TRON via Allbridge in just 7 days
→ Stablecoin card top-ups reached $13.8B cumulatively, with TRON representing 21% of August volume
→ TRON continues expanding its interoperability through integrations such as deBridge, Allbridge, WalletConnect and KiiChain

On the infrastructure side, GreatVoyage-v4.8.2 brings stronger TVM compatibility with Ethereum’s Prague and Osaka upgrades, alongside historical block-hash queries, CLZ instruction support, native Passkey verification and optimized MODEXP energy consumption.

That combination matters.

It means TRON is not simply adding accounts. It is building an environment where stablecoins, cross-chain liquidity, payments, developers and applications can operate at scale.

And with H.E. @justinsuntron continuing to represent the ecosystem in conversations around institutional adoption, global capital flows and the future of digital assets, the focus is clearly moving toward broader financial infrastructure.

The real signal is not one milestone.

It is the consistency of the activity behind them.

TRON is becoming infrastructure for moving value. 🚀

@trondao @justinsuntron #TRONEcoStar

items.title: WebAssembly Didn’t Miss the Moment. AI Was Just Late.
items.summary:
# WebAssembly Didn’t Miss the Moment. AI Was Just Late.

Share

A few years ago, WebAssembly was the format that let a game engine or a design tool like Figma run in your browser at near-native speed. It was designed around one very specific problem: Run code that you didn't review, from a source you don't fully trust — safely, instantly, and anywhere.

Now, think about what an AI agent does all day:

It writes a Python script to clean up a CSV. [...] It generates a function to call an API it found in the docs five seconds ago.

It tries something, fails, rewrites it, and tries again.

That’s code nobody reviewed, from a source nobody fully trusts, that needs to start instantly and run anywhere.

Sound familiar? The problem WebAssembly was built to solve is exactly the problem that agents just created.

Today, we're making two things official. [...] Akamai Agent Sandbox building blocks headed to Spin, the open source framework under Akamai Functions

## Why WebAssembly is a great fit for AI workloads

Where should agent-generated code run? It needs to be isolated, it needs to start fast, and it shouldn’t cost much to keep ready. Containers and VMs handle isolation well, but speed and cost are where they struggle.

WebAssembly flips that trade-off. Four properties matter most for AI and agent workloads:

items.title: What’s new in MLE 23.26.4: WebAssembly lands in Oracle AI Database | developers
items.summary:
With Release Update 23.26.4, it gains support for WebAssembly (Wasm) modules. The feature is available now on Autonomous Database, with other deployment options to follow shortly.

WebAssembly is a portable binary format for code that can run in different environments. Programs written in languages such as C, Rust, and Go can be compiled to Wasm. Now, suitable Wasm libraries can run inside Oracle AI Database and be called from MLE JavaScript. [...] To use a library, you can store its Wasm binary as an MLE module and load its JavaScript bindings as a JavaScript module. Your JavaScript code imports the Wasm module and calls the library’s functions. Those functions can then form part of an application’s database logic.

I’ll share more technical examples in the coming weeks. In the meantime, please head over to the MLE WebAssembly documentation. We also plan to update the MLE LiveLabs so you can try the feature without setting up anything! [...] What can you do with that? Image processing is one example: a Wasm library can resize an image stored in the database. Other tasks, such as optical character recognition, may also be possible with libraries whose Wasm modules and JavaScript bindings work in MLE.
